reel: Mailed kids: when US Parcel Post opened in 1913, a few families posted their children (Beagle baby, Ohio, Jan 1913; May Pierstorff, Idaho, 19 Feb 1914) until the Post Office barred humans from the mail
status: 8 source artifacts downloaded, viewed and verified (plus 4 derived crops). Rights: Smithsonian NPM photo confirmed CC0 via the Smithsonian Open Access API (media usage.access = CC0, metadata_usage CC0); two 1913 Puck chromolithographs (Library of Congress, 'No known restrictions', copyright 1913 Keppler & Schwarzmann, expired); three Chronicling America newspaper pages (LoC, public domain, pre-1930 US); 1912-13 Parcel Post stamp composite (Commons, PD US government work); May Pierstorff portrait (Commons PD-US-expired, low-res). The postalmuseum.si.edu website itself was returning 'Smithsonian site temporarily unavailable' for the whole run, so the 'Very Special Deliveries' / 'Mailing Children' exhibit text could not be read directly; facts were taken instead from the NPM object record (via api.si.edu), USPS official history, Smithsonian Magazine (Wayback copy) and the 1913-1914 newspapers themselves.

No suitable PD map found. LoC maps for Idaho 1900-1925 are almost all Sanborn fire-insurance plates (Grangeville 1901/1910 exist: loc.gov/item/sanborn01607_002) which do not show the rail route. Optional item skipped; draw the Grangeville-Lewiston route as a diagram instead.

assets.license_note: Object A.2006-22, National Postal Museum Curatorial Photographic Collection, photographer unknown. The largest file the Smithsonian serves is this 1423x2247 'High-resolution JPEG' (ids maxsize 3000 but the asset is only 2247 px tall). NOTE: the museum dates it 'c. 1900' (indexed 1890s/1900s), not 1913, and describes it as a posed humorous photo. Do not caption it as a real mailed child or as 1913.
assets.what_it_shows: A uniformed city letter carrier in a peaked cap stands against a clapboard wall with a toddler in a knitted cardigan and cap sitting inside his leather mailbag, hands on the rim, staring at the camera. Posed, humorous.
assets.best_segments: The hook. Native portrait (0.63:1), so a 9:16 crop loses only a little of the wall. Push in from the carrier's face to the baby's face; or open tight on the bag and pull out. Caption honestly: 'a posed photo, c. 1900' if any text goes on it.

assets.credit_line: 'The opening of the parcels post tunnel, January 1, 1913', Puck, 1 Jan 1913 (Keppler & Schwarzmann). Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs, LC-DIG-ppmsca-27907
assets.what_it_shows: Colour centerfold from Puck dated 1 January 1913, the day Parcel Post began: a giant scowling man ('Mount Middleman') sits on a mountain while a red train steams out of a 'Parcels Post Tunnel' from a 'Producer' farm on the left toward a 'Consumer' city on the right. Caption: 'Mount Middleman is no longer an insurmountable barrier between producer and consumer.'
assets.best_segments: COLOUR OPENER candidate for the 'January 1913, parcel post opens' beat. Landscape, so pan from the Producer farm (left) across the tunnel mouth to the Consumer city (right), or hold a 9:16 crop on the train and tunnel (centre-left).

assets.credit_line: Gordon Grant, '"Old stuff, this parcels post. Been running one myself for years!"', Puck cover, 5 Feb 1913. Library of Congress LC-DIG-ppmsca-27916
assets.what_it_shows: Colour Puck cover of 5 February 1913: a stork flies across a full moon over a snowy town carrying a baby in a bundle from its beak. Caption: 'Old stuff, this parcels post. Been running one myself for years!' A period joke about babies and the new parcel post, printed two weeks after the Beagle baby story.
assets.best_segments: Perfect comic beat for 'families mailed their babies'. Portrait, near 9:16 after cropping the masthead. Push in on the bundle/baby; the moon makes a strong colour frame.

assets.credit_line: Charlotte May Pierstorff, c. 1914, via National Postal Museum / Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
assets.what_it_shows: Head-and-shoulders halftone portrait of a blonde girl of about five with a large hair bow and a white dress, looking slightly off-camera. Identified as Charlotte May Pierstorff (1908-1987).
assets.best_segments: The 'person' beat: 'May Pierstorff, five years old'. Portrait, 9:16-ready; keep it under 2 s and avoid heavy zoom because of the resolution.

assets.license: Public domain (US newspaper published 1914; Library of Congress Chronicling America, no known restrictions)
assets.credit_line: Idaho County Free Press (Grangeville, Idaho), 19 Feb 1914, p. 1. Library of Congress, Chronicling America
assets.what_it_shows: Front page of the Grangeville paper printed the very day May was mailed. Bottom-centre article: 'Little Girl Sent By Mail As Parcel Post Package' with the sub-head 'May Pierstorff, five years old, to visit grandmother bedecked with postage stamps by Uncle Sam'.
assets.best_segments: Document beat. Start on the masthead 'IDAHO COUNTY FREE PRESS ... FEBRUARY 19, 1914' then whip down to the article; or use the _cliparticle crop directly.

assets.credit_line: Idaho County Free Press, 19 Feb 1914, p. 1 (Library of Congress)
assets.what_it_shows: Readable clip of the article: headline, sub-head and the text '...was sent from Grangeville to Lewiston on today's train as parcels post mail. The postage bill for the little girl and her suitcase was 53 cents. The entire "package" weighed 49 pounds.'
assets.best_segments: Hold 2-3 s with a slow push on '53 cents' / '49 pounds'. Landscape-ish (1.17:1): in 9:16 use a vertical pan from headline to the price line.

assets.license: Public domain (US newspaper published 1914; Library of Congress Chronicling America, no known restrictions)
assets.credit_line: The Shoshone Journal (Shoshone, Idaho), 27 Feb 1914, p. 1. Library of Congress, Chronicling America
assets.what_it_shows: Front page; bottom-right column item 'BARS BABIES FROM THE MAIL. Ruling of Department has Bearing on Grangeville Case.' reporting that Second Assistant Postmaster General Stewart ruled all human beings and live animals barred from the mails, the queen bee being the only exception.
assets.best_segments: The 'ban' beat. Use the _cliparticle crop; zoom on 'BARS BABIES FROM THE MAIL' then on 'queen bee'.

assets.credit_line: The Shoshone Journal, 27 Feb 1914, p. 1 (Library of Congress)
assets.what_it_shows: Readable clip: 'BARS BABIES FROM THE MAIL' headline and the full ruling paragraph.
assets.best_segments: Near-square; in 9:16 pan top to bottom over about 2 s.
